cards.front: In a newborn with hyperammonemia, how does urine orotic acid separate OTC deficiency from CPS-I deficiency?
cards.back: **OTC deficiency** (X-linked, most common urea cycle defect): unused **carbamoyl phosphate** spills into pyrimidine synthesis, so **orotic acid is high**. **CPS-I deficiency** (autosomal recessive): no carbamoyl phosphate is made, so **orotic acid is low or normal**.
cards.back_pt: **Deficiência de OTC** (ligada ao X, o defeito do ciclo da ureia mais comum): o **carbamoil fosfato** não usado desvia para a síntese de pirimidinas, e o **ácido orótico fica alto**. **Deficiência de CPS-I** (autossômica recessiva): não se forma carbamoil fosfato, e o **ácido orótico fica baixo ou normal**.

cards.front: Why is a high blood ammonia toxic to the brain?
cards.back: Astrocytes clear ammonia by making **glutamate** and then **glutamine**. Glutamine builds up and pulls in water: **astrocyte swelling** and **cerebral edema**. Using up **α-ketoglutarate** also slows the **TCA cycle**. Signs: vomiting, lethargy, **asterixis**, slurred speech, coma.
cards.back_pt: Os astrócitos removem a amônia formando **glutamato** e depois **glutamina**. A glutamina se acumula e atrai água: **edema dos astrócitos** e **edema cerebral**. O consumo de **α-cetoglutarato** também retarda o **ciclo de Krebs**. Sinais: vômitos, letargia, **asterixe** (*flapping*), fala arrastada, coma.

cards.front: What enzyme defect causes classic phenylketonuria (PKU), and what are its key features?
cards.back: **Phenylalanine hydroxylase** deficiency (a rarer form is a **BH4** cofactor defect). Phenylalanine builds up and **tyrosine becomes essential**. Untreated: intellectual disability, seizures, **fair skin and hair**, eczema and a **musty odor**. Treat with a low-phenylalanine diet.
cards.back_pt: Deficiência de **fenilalanina hidroxilase** (uma forma mais rara é o defeito do cofator **BH4**). A fenilalanina se acumula e a **tirosina se torna essencial**. Sem tratamento: deficiência intelectual, convulsões, **pele e cabelos claros**, eczema e **odor de mofo** (*musty odor*). Tratar com dieta pobre em fenilalanina.

cards.front: What is alkaptonuria, and how does it present?
cards.back: Autosomal recessive deficiency of **homogentisate oxidase** in tyrosine breakdown. **Homogentisic acid** accumulates: **urine turns black on standing**, dark blue-black pigment in ear cartilage and sclera (**ochronosis**), and degenerative **arthropathy** of the spine and large joints.
cards.back_pt: Deficiência autossômica recessiva da **homogentisato oxidase** na degradação da tirosina. O **ácido homogentísico** se acumula: **urina que escurece quando deixada em repouso**, pigmento negro-azulado na cartilagem da orelha e na esclera (**ocronose**) e **artropatia** degenerativa da coluna e das grandes articulações.

cards.front: How does homocystinuria differ from Marfan syndrome, given that both cause a tall, thin body and lens dislocation?
cards.back: **Homocystinuria** (most often **cystathionine β-synthase** deficiency): lens displaced **downward**, intellectual disability and **thrombosis**. **Marfan** (fibrillin-1): lens displaced **upward**, normal intelligence and aortic root dilation. In homocystinuria, **cysteine becomes essential**.
cards.back_pt: **Homocistinúria** (mais frequentemente deficiência de **cistationina β-sintase**): cristalino deslocado **para baixo**, deficiência intelectual e **trombose**. **Marfan** (fibrilina-1): cristalino deslocado **para cima**, inteligência normal e dilatação da raiz da aorta. Na homocistinúria, a **cisteína se torna essencial**.

cards.front: Which enzyme is defective in maple syrup urine disease, and what builds up?
cards.back: **Branched-chain α-ketoacid dehydrogenase** (a **thiamine**-dependent complex). **Leucine, isoleucine and valine** and their ketoacids build up. Newborns have poor feeding, vomiting, **encephalopathy** and urine with a **sweet, burnt-sugar odor**.
cards.back_pt: **Desidrogenase de α-cetoácidos de cadeia ramificada** (complexo dependente de **tiamina**). **Leucina, isoleucina e valina** e seus cetoácidos se acumulam. O recém-nascido tem dificuldade de alimentação, vômitos, **encefalopatia** e urina com **odor adocicado, de açúcar queimado**.

cards.front: Why does HGPRT deficiency (Lesch-Nyhan syndrome) raise uric acid?
cards.back: **HGPRT** salvages **hypoxanthine** and **guanine** back into nucleotides. Without it, these bases are broken down to **uric acid**. Unused **PRPP** accumulates and drives more **de novo purine synthesis**, which adds even more uric acid.
cards.back_pt: A **HGPRT** reaproveita **hipoxantina** e **guanina** pela via de salvamento, convertendo-as de volta em nucleotídeos. Sem ela, essas bases são degradadas a **ácido úrico**. O **PRPP** não usado se acumula e estimula mais **síntese de purinas de novo**, o que aumenta ainda mais o ácido úrico.

cards.front: Which nucleotide-synthesis enzymes do mycophenolate, ribavirin and leflunomide inhibit?
cards.back: **Mycophenolate** and **ribavirin**: **IMP dehydrogenase**, so cells make less **GMP/GTP** (purines). **Leflunomide**: **dihydroorotate dehydrogenase**, so cells make less pyrimidine. Mycophenolate and leflunomide hit **activated lymphocytes** hardest, because these cells depend on de novo synthesis.
cards.back_pt: **Micofenolato** e **ribavirina**: **IMP desidrogenase**, e a célula produz menos **GMP/GTP** (purinas). **Leflunomida**: **di-hidro-orotato desidrogenase**, e a célula produz menos pirimidinas. Micofenolato e leflunomida afetam mais os **linfócitos ativados**, que dependem da síntese de novo.

questions.stem: A 3-day-old boy, born at term after a normal pregnancy, fed well for the first 2 days. He is now vomiting, feeding poorly and very sleepy. He breathes fast. Arterial blood gas shows pH 7.50, PaCO2 28 mm Hg and HCO3 21 mEq/L. Serum glucose is normal, the anion gap is normal, and there are no ketones in the urine. Plasma ammonia is markedly elevated, BUN is low and plasma citrulline is low. Urine orotic acid is markedly elevated. Which enzyme is most likely deficient?
questions.explanation: Hyperammonemia with **respiratory alkalosis**, low BUN and low citrulline points to a urea cycle block before citrulline. **High orotic acid** means carbamoyl phosphate is made but cannot join ornithine, so it spills into pyrimidine synthesis: **OTC deficiency**. In **CPS-I** (and N-acetylglutamate synthase) deficiency, no carbamoyl phosphate is made, so orotic acid is low or normal. Argininosuccinate synthetase deficiency would make citrulline high, not low. UMP synthase deficiency raises orotic acid but causes megaloblastic anemia, not hyperammonemia.
questions.explanation_pt: Hiperamonemia com **alcalose respiratória**, ureia baixa e citrulina baixa indica bloqueio do ciclo da ureia antes da citrulina. O **ácido orótico alto** mostra que o carbamoil fosfato é formado, mas não se une à ornitina, e desvia para a síntese de pirimidinas: **deficiência de OTC**. Na deficiência de **CPS-I** (e de N-acetilglutamato sintase) não se forma carbamoil fosfato, então o ácido orótico fica baixo ou normal. A deficiência de argininossuccinato sintetase elevaria a citrulina, e não a reduziria. A deficiência de UMP sintase eleva o ácido orótico, mas causa anemia megaloblástica, e não hiperamonemia.

questions.stem: An 18-month-old boy is evaluated for motor delay. He cannot sit without support and has involuntary writhing movements of the arms. In recent weeks he has started biting his lips and fingers, causing wounds. His mother has noticed orange, sand-like crystals in his diapers. Serum uric acid is elevated. A maternal uncle had similar problems. Deficiency of which enzyme best explains these findings?
questions.explanation: **Self-mutilation**, writhing movements (choreoathetosis/dystonia), developmental delay and **orange uric acid crystals** in a boy with an affected maternal uncle (X-linked) is **Lesch-Nyhan syndrome**: **HGPRT** deficiency blocks purine salvage, so uric acid rises. Xanthine oxidase makes uric acid, so its deficiency would lower uric acid. APRT deficiency causes kidney stones of 2,8-dihydroxyadenine without neurologic disease, and ADA deficiency causes SCID.
questions.explanation_pt: **Automutilação**, movimentos coreoatetoides/distonia, atraso do desenvolvimento e **cristais alaranjados de ácido úrico** em um menino com tio materno afetado (ligado ao X) indicam **síndrome de Lesch-Nyhan**: a deficiência de **HGPRT** bloqueia a **via de salvamento** (*salvage*) das purinas, e o ácido úrico sobe. A xantina oxidase produz ácido úrico, então sua deficiência baixaria o ácido úrico. A deficiência de APRT causa cálculos renais de 2,8-di-hidroxiadenina sem doença neurológica, e a deficiência de ADA causa SCID (imunodeficiência combinada grave).

questions.stem: A 9-month-old girl recently moved with her family from a region without newborn screening. She has developmental delay and has had two seizures. Her skin and hair are much lighter than her parents' and she has eczema. Her urine has a musty odor. Plasma phenylalanine is markedly elevated, plasma tyrosine is low, and the biopterin profile is normal. Besides restricting phenylalanine, which amino acid must now be supplied in her diet?
questions.explanation: This is classic **PKU** from **phenylalanine hydroxylase** deficiency (normal biopterin excludes a BH4 defect). The enzyme normally makes **tyrosine** from phenylalanine, so tyrosine **becomes essential** and is needed for catecholamines and melanin (hence the fair skin). Cysteine becomes essential in homocystinuria, not in PKU, because it is made from homocysteine through cystathionine.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de **PKU** clássica por deficiência de **fenilalanina hidroxilase** (biopterina normal exclui defeito de BH4). A enzima normalmente produz **tirosina** a partir da fenilalanina, então a tirosina **se torna essencial**, sendo necessária para catecolaminas e melanina (daí a pele clara). A cisteína se torna essencial na homocistinúria, e não na PKU, pois é produzida a partir da homocisteína via cistationina.

questions.stem: A 14-year-old boy is tall and thin with long arms and fingers. He has a mild learning disability and blurred vision. Slit-lamp exam shows both lenses displaced downward and inward. Two months ago he had a deep vein thrombosis of the left leg without a clear trigger. Echocardiography shows a normal aortic root. Plasma homocysteine and plasma methionine are both markedly elevated. Which enzyme is most likely deficient?
questions.explanation: A marfanoid boy with **downward lens dislocation**, learning disability and **venous thrombosis** has **homocystinuria**. High homocysteine **plus high methionine** means homocysteine cannot move forward to cystathionine, so **cystathionine β-synthase** is deficient. Defects of methionine synthase or MTHFR also raise homocysteine, but they block remethylation, so methionine is low or normal. Marfan syndrome displaces the lens upward and spares intelligence.
questions.explanation_pt: Um menino marfanoide com **luxação do cristalino para baixo**, dificuldade de aprendizado e **trombose venosa** tem **homocistinúria**. Homocisteína alta **com metionina alta** mostra que a homocisteína não consegue seguir para cistationina, logo há deficiência de **cistationina β-sintase**. Defeitos da metionina sintase ou da MTHFR também elevam a homocisteína, mas bloqueiam a remetilação, então a metionina fica baixa ou normal. Na síndrome de Marfan, o cristalino desloca-se para cima e a inteligência é normal.

notes.title: Amino acid and nucleotide metabolism: urea cycle, inborn errors and nucleotide synthesis
notes.body_md:
## Essential amino acids

- Must come from the diet: **phenylalanine, valine, threonine, tryptophan, isoleucine, methionine, histidine, leucine, lysine**.
- **Leucine** and **lysine** are purely ketogenic.
- **Tyrosine** becomes essential in **PKU**; **cysteine** becomes essential in **homocystinuria**.

## Urea cycle

- **CPS-I** (mitochondria, activated by **N-acetylglutamate**) makes carbamoyl phosphate. **OTC** joins it to ornithine to form citrulline.
- Urea cycle defects: hyperammonemia, vomiting, lethargy, respiratory alkalosis, low BUN.
- **OTC deficiency**: high **orotic acid**. **CPS-I deficiency**: orotic acid low or normal.
- Treatment: low-protein diet and nitrogen scavengers (**sodium benzoate**, **phenylbutyrate**). Lactulose and rifaximin for hyperammonemia in liver disease are in the GI blocks.

## Other inborn errors

- **PKU**, **alkaptonuria** (dark urine on standing), **homocystinuria** (lens down, thrombosis) and **maple syrup urine disease** (leucine, isoleucine, valine).
- **Albinism** (tyrosinase defect) is covered with skin; **cystinuria** stones with renal.

## Special products

- **Tyrosine**: catecholamines, thyroid hormone, melanin.
- **Tryptophan**: serotonin, melatonin and **niacin**.
- **Histidine**: histamine. **Glycine**: heme (with succinyl-CoA). **Arginine**: **nitric oxide**, creatine, urea.

## Nucleotide synthesis

- **Purines** are built on **PRPP** and pass through **IMP**. **Pyrimidines**: the ring (**orotate**) is made first, then joined to PRPP.
- Salvage: **HGPRT** deficiency causes **Lesch-Nyhan** (X-linked, self-mutilation, high uric acid; gout in the arthritis block).
- **ADA deficiency**: toxic deoxyadenosine metabolites kill lymphocytes and cause **SCID**.
- **Orotic aciduria** (UMP synthase): megaloblastic anemia that does not respond to B12 or folate, with no hyperammonemia.

## Drug targets

- **Mycophenolate**, **ribavirin**: IMP dehydrogenase. **Leflunomide**: dihydroorotate dehydrogenase.
- **Methotrexate**, **5-FU**, **hydroxyurea**: see heme-onc pharmacology. One-carbon (folate, B12) chemistry: see the vitamins block.
notes.body_pt_md:
## Aminoácidos essenciais

- Precisam vir da dieta: **fenilalanina, valina, treonina, triptofano, isoleucina, metionina, histidina, leucina, lisina**.
- **Leucina** e **lisina** são exclusivamente cetogênicas.
- A **tirosina** se torna essencial na **PKU**; a **cisteína** se torna essencial na **homocistinúria**.

## Ciclo da ureia

- A **CPS-I** (mitocôndria, ativada pelo **N-acetilglutamato**) forma carbamoil fosfato. A **OTC** o une à ornitina, formando citrulina.
- Defeitos do ciclo da ureia: hiperamonemia, vômitos, letargia, alcalose respiratória, ureia baixa.
- **Deficiência de OTC**: **ácido orótico** alto. **Deficiência de CPS-I**: ácido orótico baixo ou normal.
- Tratamento: dieta pobre em proteínas e captadores de nitrogênio (**benzoato de sódio**, **fenilbutirato**). Lactulose e rifaximina, usadas na hiperamonemia da doença hepática, estão nos blocos de GI.

## Outros erros inatos

- **PKU**, **alcaptonúria** (urina que escurece quando deixada em repouso), **homocistinúria** (cristalino para baixo, trombose) e **doença da urina em xarope de bordo** (leucina, isoleucina, valina).
- O **albinismo** (defeito da tirosinase) está com a pele; os cálculos da **cistinúria**, com o renal.

## Produtos especiais

- **Tirosina**: catecolaminas, hormônio tireoidiano, melanina.
- **Triptofano**: serotonina, melatonina e **niacina**.
- **Histidina**: histamina. **Glicina**: heme (com succinil-CoA). **Arginina**: **óxido nítrico**, creatina, ureia.

## Síntese de nucleotídeos

- As **purinas** são montadas sobre o **PRPP** e passam pelo **IMP**. **Pirimidinas**: o anel (**orotato**) é feito primeiro e depois unido ao PRPP.
- Via de salvamento (*salvage*): a deficiência de **HGPRT** causa **Lesch-Nyhan** (ligada ao X, automutilação, ácido úrico alto; gota no bloco de artrites).
- **Deficiência de ADA**: metabólitos tóxicos da desoxiadenosina matam linfócitos e causam **SCID**.
- **Acidúria orótica** (UMP sintase): anemia megaloblástica que não responde a B12 nem a folato, sem hiperamonemia.

## Alvos de fármacos

- **Micofenolato**, **ribavirina**: IMP desidrogenase. **Leflunomida**: di-hidro-orotato desidrogenase.
- **Metotrexato**, **5-FU**, **hidroxiureia**: ver farmacologia de hemato-oncologia. Química de um carbono (folato, B12): ver o bloco de vitaminas.
